source.title: Interplay Between Optimization and Generalization of Stochastic Gradient Descent with Covariance Noise
source.authors: Yeming Wen; Kevin Luk; M. Gazeau; Guodong Zhang; Harris Chan; Jimmy Ba

record.file_problem: The supplied text is a full paper, but its title differs from the metadata title: the text is “An Empirical Study of Large-Batch Stochastic Gradient Descent with Structured Covariance Noise.”
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports training-error outcomes for ResNet44 on CIFAR-10 under several large- and small-batch SGD noise conditions, bearing on V1, but it does not test the claim’s full set of recipes or benchmarks.
record.gate_note: Figure 3 reports training error per parameter update for the listed regimes. Training error values are presented only in the figure; no numeric values can be extracted from the text. Validation-accuracy results and cited findings are not rows because they do not measure training classification error.
record.test_reason: Figure 3 measures training classification error for ResNet44 on CIFAR-10 under different batch sizes and noise conditions, bearing on V1 in a new training setting. The supplied text does not preserve readable curve values or establish near-zero final training error.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that diagonal Fisher noise improves large-batch generalization while retaining desirable convergence, approximately matching ordinary large-batch convergence in the ResNet44 CIFAR-10 comparison. They also conclude that noise covariance structure is more informative about optimization than gradient variance alone.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares large-batch SGD with and without injected covariance noise, and small-batch SGD; it uses Ghost Batch Normalization for large-batch regimes. The V1 claim concerns reaching near-zero training error across specified benchmarks and conditions, but the supplied text does not state the plotted training-error values.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported training-error comparison varies batch regime and injected noise covariance structure.

fits_no_version.finding: Diagonal Fisher noise preserves approximately the convergence speed of ordinary large-batch training, while full Fisher noise and small-batch training converge more slowly despite similar gradient variance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Noise covariance structure affects training convergence beyond what gradient variance predicts.

fits_no_version.finding: Diagonal Fisher noise improves validation accuracy over ordinary large-batch training and lowers the final model's maximum Hessian eigenvalue.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Structured gradient noise can improve large-batch generalization and alter final curvature.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 23rd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS 2020), PMLR Volume 108
record.problems: Training-error outcomes are shown in Figure 3 without text-stated numeric values. The reported comparison is limited to ResNet44 on CIFAR-10 and does not establish whether training error is near zero.
record.rows_left_out: No rows retained: Figure 3 is the only reported training-error comparison relevant to V1, but its values are figure-only and the supplied text does not provide extractable values. Validation accuracy in Table 2 measures a different outcome.

untested.parts: Near-zero final training error cannot be assessed from the supplied figure text. Corrupted or random labels, CIFAR-100 training error, Adam, model-size comparisons, early stopping and regularization comparisons are not tested.

record.verdict_notes: There are no extracted rows to fix. Figure 3 is explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so it is not an undeclared missing result. Relative convergence speed and the statement that full Fisher has poor convergence after 8000 updates do not establish whether V1's near-zero-error criterion holds. No verdict is justified from the supplied text. Ghost Batch Normalization is held in the large-batch recipes rather than compared against training without normalization.

versions.untested_parts: The text does not state the training-error values needed to assess near-zero error; it does not test corrupted or random labels, smaller models, early stopping, Adam, or CIFAR-100 training error.
